rows.col_1: POST https://developer.api.autodesk.com/construction/assets/v2/projects/{projectId}/assets:batch-get
user context required
data:read
JSON
Must be Bearer <token>, where <token> is obtained via a three-legged OAuth flow.
Must be application/json
The Forma project ID. Must be a UUID or a project ID of the form “b.{UUID}”.

Specifies whether or not returned assets include custom attributes or not. If true, they’re included. If
false, they’re not. Default is false.
Whether or not soft-deleted object should be included in the response. If true, soft-deleted objects are returned. If false, they are not. The default is false.
An array of unique IDs of assets to fetch.
Successfully returned a batch of assets.
The request could not be understood by the server due to malformed syntax or missing request header
The request was not accepted because it lacked valid authentication credentials
The request was not accepted because the client is authenticated, but is not authorized to access the target resource
The resource cannot be found
The request was not accepted because the rate limit was exceeded due to too many requests being made.
An unexpected error occurred on the server
Returned assets
The ID of the component.
The time when the component was created (ISO8601 Date time format in UTC).
The actor that created the component. This is an Autodesk / Oxygen ID.
The time when the component was last updated (ISO8601 Date time format in UTC).
The actor that last updated the component. This is an Autodesk / Oxygen ID.
The time when the component was deleted at (ISO8601 Date time format in UTC).
The actor that deleted the component. This is an Autodesk / Oxygen ID.
A flag indicating whether the component is active or inactive (isActive is true if-and-only-if deletedAt is empty).

A global sequence number that is incremented any time a component of this type is created, updated, or deleted. If you cache components, you can use the version value to compare the cached component to the same component online to see if the component has been updated. If the online component has a higher version value, it has been updated.

An identifying name for the asset such as “laundry 220V outlet”. The name need not be unique, and shouldn’t be confused with the asset ‘id’ field, which is created and assigned when the asset is created. This value appears as “Asset ID” in the Assets UI, and may sometimes be called “Name” in asset exports.
The ID of the category to which the asset belongs.
The ID of the status assigned to the asset. The status must belong to the status set specified by the asset’s category.
A brief description of the asset. Currently limited to 1000 characters.
The ID of the location of the asset. This value is supplied through the Locations API.
A string that lists a barcode value that may be assigned to the asset. The string uses whatever format your barcode system supports.

An optional JSON dictionary specifying one or more custom attributes and values to be assigned to the
asset. The custom attributes must belong to the set of custom attributes specified by the asset’s category.
The dictionary is a set of key:value pairs that each starts with the unique custom attribute name (not to
be confused with the custom attribute’s display name) followed by the attribute value. The value must use
the data type defined by the attribute:
For text, the value is a string.
For date, the value is an ISO8601 date string with no time, for example, “2020-04-10”.
For select, the value is a valid ID from the list of values defined for this custom attribute.
For multi-select, the value is an array of valid IDs from the list of values defined for this custom attribute.
For boolean, the value is a boolean.
For numeric, the value is a string that parses as a valid floating point number (not localized).

A String value
Max length: 250
An array of String values
A Boolean value
The ID of the company to which the creating user belongs in the project.
